newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-SMALL TAKES CAREER BEST TO BOOST WARWICKSHIRE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SMALL TAKES CAREER BEST TO BOOST WARWICKSHIRE.

text.p: Warwickshire's former England pace bowler Gladstone Small showed a return to his form of earlier years with a career Sunday league best of five for 26 to destroy Middlesex at Edgbaston.
Only wicketkeeper Keith Brown showed any real resistance with an unbeaten 44 as Middlesex collapsed to be all out for 114 in 32.5 overs after Warwickshire had made 222 for five.
The win moved Warwickshire up into fourth place.

In contrast, there was a run feast at Trent Bridge where Nottinghamshire's Paul Johnson and Graeme Archer both made centuries as a total of 530 runs were scored in their 32-run defeat of neighbours Derbyshire.
Johnson hit 11 fours and a six in making 117 while Archer was undefeated with 104 as Nottinghamshire reached 280 for six in their 40 overs.
Led by a dashing 121 by England hopeful Chris Adams, Derby made a spirited reply but in the end fell short, mustering only 248 for seven in their allotted overs.
A century by Jason Gallian helped keep Lancashire's 100 percent record intact as they stayed top of the Sunday league with a 75-run win over Northamptonshire at Old Trafford.

Gallian's 101 not out contained nine fours and a six as Lancashire made 241 for six. England reject seamer Peter Martin made victory certain with a haul of five for 21 as Northants were dismissed for 166.
